newsitem.title: EGYPT: Lower prices on Cairo bourse seen climbing soon.
newsitem.headline: Lower prices on Cairo bourse seen climbing soon.

text.p: Alexandria National Iron and Steel had the highest turnover in terms of value on the Cairo bourse on Thursday, and one broker predicted a general trend for prices to climb.

The company was on a list of firms the Egyptian government released in February which the state said it intended to sell under its fast-moving privatisation programme. It said it would sell five percent of Alexandria National Iron and Steel. It held 65 percent.
The partly private company and German firm Messer Griesheim on Thursday signed a $25 million deal to set up a joint venture firm to produce industrial gases in the Mediterranean city of Alexandria.
Alexandria iron's share fell 13.7 pounds to close at 260.78 in turnover of 22 million pounds, part of the bourse's total 91.84 million ($27 million) turnover.
The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) said the index ended at 364.15 points. Out of the 89 shares traded, 33 ended up, 38 fell and 18 were unchanged.
"There is decreased demand. Institutions which have been such a big part of the market until now are wary. They want to see where the market will bottom out," said broker Tarek Lotfy of Intercapital.
"I don't see prices going much lower and the general trend will be on the upside," he predicted.

Egypt Arab African Bank/EAAB share closed 1.28 higher at 27.05 pounds in turnover of 12.46 million pounds. The bank said on Wednesday it raised net profits in calendar 1996 by eight percent to 11.506 million pounds ($3.39 million) from 10.575 million in the previous year.
The profits are equivalent to about 1.5 pounds for each of the 7.5 million shares.
For the second day, Cairo Precision Industries had high turnover with shares worth 11 million pounds changing hands. Its share fell 4.5 pounds to close at 132.
Helwan Portland Cement shares fell 0.35 pounds to 74.7 in trade worth 4.87 million pounds.
The milling sector was represented by Central and West Delta Flour Mills, which rose 1.39 pounds to 89.5 in turnover worth 4.76 million.
Lotfy said many investors were waiting to see how the introduction of the private sector into milling would go before they committed themselves.

"People are not able to differentiate which is going to be able to succeed in the face of competition. The worry is that the private sector will increase competition snd take away the market share," he said.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 522.06 points from 524.78 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms fell to 263.01 from 269.56.
